subject: math
title: Greatest Common Factor and Lowest Common Multiple
seo_title: Grade 7 GCF and LCM Worksheets: Greatest Common Factor and Lowest Common Multiple (Free, Answer Key)
standard_text: Determine the greatest common factor of whole numbers up to 144 and the lowest common multiple of two or three whole numbers, using a variety of tools and strategies
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 math worksheets for the Ontario curriculum: factors and common factors, the greatest common factor with lists and factor trees, multiples, the lowest common multiple of two or three numbers, and GCF or LCM word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: The GCF is the biggest number that divides all the numbers. The LCM is the first number they all divide into.
key_sub: For 6 and 8: the GCF is 2 and the LCM is 24, not 6 × 8 = 48. Use the GCF for equal groups, rows and pieces, and the LCM for things that repeat and line up, like buses or hot dogs and buns.
body_html:
The greatest common factor (GCF)

A common factor divides two or more numbers with no remainder. The greatest common factor is the biggest one. List the factors of each number, circle the ones in every list, and pick the greatest.

Example

Find the GCF of 54 and 90.

Factors of 54: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18, 27, 54. Factors of 90: 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 9, 10, 15, 18, 30, 45, 90. Common factors: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18.

Answer: 18

The GCF with factor trees

For bigger numbers, split each number into primes with a factor tree. The GCF is the product of the primes that the numbers share. Use a shared prime as many times as it appears in both lists.

Example

Find the GCF of 72 and 120.

Shared primes: 2, 2, 2 and 3. Multiply them: 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 = 24. Check: 72 = 24 × 3 and 120 = 24 × 5.

Answer: 24

The lowest common multiple (LCM)

A common multiple is in the skip-counting list of every number. The lowest common multiple is the first one. Count by the biggest number and stop at the first number the others divide into.

Example

Find the LCM of 4, 6 and 10.

Count by 10: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60. 20 is not a multiple of 6, 30 is not a multiple of 4, but 60 = 4 × 15 = 6 × 10.

Answer: 60

With prime factorizations, use each prime the greatest number of times it appears in any one number. 12 = 2 × 2 × 3 and 18 = 2 × 3 × 3, so the LCM is 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 = 36.

GCF or LCM?

The problem asks…UseExample
The greatest number of identical groups, bags or teamsGCF120 water bottles and 84 granola bars make 12 bags
The biggest equal rows, pieces or squares with nothing left overGCF96 and 72 chairs: rows of 24
When repeating events happen together againLCMBuses every 12 and 18 minutes: 36 minutes
The least number to buy so pack sizes matchLCMHot dogs in 12s, buns in 8s: 24 of each

Check your answer: a GCF is never bigger than the smallest number, and an LCM is never smaller than the biggest number.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Stopping at any common factor: GCF of 36 and 90 is 9Find the greatest one: 18
Multiplying for the LCM: LCM of 6 and 8 is 4848 is a common multiple, but 24 comes first
Multiplying three numbers: LCM of 4, 6 and 8 is 192Count by 8: 8, 16, 24. The LCM is 24
Mixing up GCF and LCMGroups, rows and pieces: GCF. Repeating and matching: LCM
Using only two of three numbersCheck that the answer works for every number
Using a shared prime only once72 and 120 share 2 × 2 × 2 × 3, so the GCF is 24, not 6

faq.q: How do you find the GCF of two numbers?
faq.a: List the factors of each number and pick the greatest one that is in both lists, or multiply the prime factors the numbers share. For 72 and 120, the GCF is 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 = 24.

faq.q: How do you find the LCM of three numbers?
faq.a: Count by the biggest number until you reach a number the other two also divide. For 4, 6 and 10, count 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60; 60 is a multiple of 4 and 6, so the LCM is 60.

faq.q: How do you know whether to use GCF or LCM in a word problem?
faq.a: Use the GCF when you split things into the greatest number of identical groups or the biggest equal rows or pieces. Use the LCM when events repeat and line up again, or when you buy packs so two amounts match, like hot dogs and buns.

faq.q: Is GCF and LCM in the Ontario Grade 7 math curriculum?
faq.a: Yes. Expectation B2.6 of the Ontario Grade 7 math curriculum asks students to find the greatest common factor of whole numbers up to 144 and the lowest common multiple of two or three whole numbers. LCM in Ontario stands for lowest common multiple, which is the same as least common multiple.

items.q: Which list shows all the factors of 36?
items.e: Find the factor pairs: 1 × 36, 2 × 18, 3 × 12, 4 × 9, 6 × 6. So the factors of 36 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36. Check every number from 1 up to the pair that meets in the middle, and include 1 and 36.

items.q: Which list shows all the factors of 48?
items.e: Find the factor pairs: 1 × 48, 2 × 24, 3 × 16, 4 × 12, 6 × 8. So the factors of 48 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 48. Check every number from 1 up to the pair that meets in the middle, and include 1 and 48.

items.q: Which list shows all the factors of 84?
items.e: Find the factor pairs: 1 × 84, 2 × 42, 3 × 28, 4 × 21, 6 × 14, 7 × 12. So the factors of 84 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 12, 14, 21, 28, 42, 84. Check every number from 1 up to the pair that meets in the middle, and include 1 and 84.

items.q: How many factors does 64 have?
items.e: The factors of 64 are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64. That is 7 factors. Counting 8 twice gives 8. Counting pairs gives 4. Leaving out 1 and 64 gives 5.

items.q: How many factors does 90 have?
items.e: The factors of 90 are 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 9, 10, 15, 18, 30, 45, 90. That is 12 factors. Counting pairs gives 6. Leaving out 1 and 90 gives 10. 4 is the number of primes in 2 × 3 × 3 × 5.

items.q: Which number is a factor of 126?
items.e: 14 × 9 = 126, so 14 is a factor of 126. 252 is a multiple of 126, not a factor. 126 ÷ 12 and 126 ÷ 16 have remainders.

items.q: Which number is a factor of 144?
items.e: 18 × 8 = 144, so 18 is a factor of 144. 288 is a multiple of 144, not a factor. 144 ÷ 14 and 144 ÷ 21 have remainders.

items.q: Which number is not a factor of 108?
Which number is not a factor of 132?
Which list shows all the common factors of 24 and 40?
items.e: Factors of 24: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. Factors of 40: 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 20, 40. The numbers in both lists are 1, 2, 4, 8. Keep 1 and the greatest one.

items.q: Which list shows all the common factors of 36 and 60?
items.e: Factors of 36: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36. Factors of 60: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 10, 12, 15, 20, 30, 60. The numbers in both lists are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. Keep 1 and the greatest one.

items.q: Which list shows all the common factors of 42 and 56?
items.e: Factors of 42: 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 14, 21, 42. Factors of 56: 1, 2, 4, 7, 8, 14, 28, 56. The numbers in both lists are 1, 2, 7, 14. Keep 1 and the greatest one.

items.q: Which list shows all the common factors of 45 and 75?
items.e: Factors of 45: 1, 3, 5, 9, 15, 45. Factors of 75: 1, 3, 5, 15, 25, 75. The numbers in both lists are 1, 3, 5, 15. Keep 1 and the greatest one.

items.q: Which number is a common factor of 54 and 72?
items.e: 9 × 6 = 54 and 9 × 8 = 72, so 9 is a common factor. 4 is a factor of 72 only, 27 is a factor of 54 only, and 216 is a common multiple.

items.q: Which number is a common factor of 70 and 98?
items.e: 14 × 5 = 70 and 14 × 7 = 98, so 14 is a common factor. 5 is a factor of 70 only, 49 is a factor of 98 only, and 490 is a common multiple.

items.q: Which number is not a common factor of 48 and 80?
items.e: 6 is a factor of 48, but 80 ÷ 6 = 13 R 2, so 6 is not a common factor. 4, 8 and 16 divide both numbers.

items.q: Which number is not a common factor of 60 and 90?
items.e: 4 is a factor of 60, but 90 ÷ 4 = 22 R 2, so 4 is not a common factor. 5, 6 and 15 divide both numbers.

items.q: These are the factor pairs of 120: 1 × 120, 2 × 60, 3 × 40, 4 × 30, 5 × 24, 6 × 20, 8 × ?, 10 × 12. What is the missing number?
items.e: 8 × 15 = 120, so the missing number is 15. 8 × 14 = 112 and 8 × 16 = 128. 12 is already in the pair 10 × 12.

items.q: Aiden says 7 is a common factor of 28 and 63. Is he right?
items.e: 7 divides both numbers with no remainder: 28 = 7 × 4 and 63 = 7 × 9. So 7 is a common factor. A number can be a common factor of an even and an odd number.

items.q: Noah says 32 is a common factor of 56 and 96, because 32 is a factor of 96. Is he right?
c: No. 32 is not a factor of 56
items.e: A common factor must divide both numbers. 96 = 32 × 3, but 56 ÷ 32 = 1 R 24. So 32 is not a common factor. The common factors of 56 and 96 are 1, 2, 4, 8.

items.q: What is the greatest common factor (GCF) of 32 and 48?
items.e: Factors of 32: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32. Factors of 48: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 48. Common factors: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. The greatest is 16. 8 is a common factor too, but not the greatest. 96 is the LCM.

items.q: What is the greatest common factor (GCF) of 45 and 60?
items.e: Factors of 45: 1, 3, 5, 9, 15, 45. Factors of 60: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 10, 12, 15, 20, 30, 60. Common factors: 1, 3, 5, 15. The greatest is 15. 5 is a common factor too, but not the greatest. 180 is the LCM.

items.q: What is the greatest common factor (GCF) of 56 and 84?
items.e: Factors of 56: 1, 2, 4, 7, 8, 14, 28, 56. Factors of 84: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 12, 14, 21, 28, 42, 84. Common factors: 1, 2, 4, 7, 14, 28. The greatest is 28. 14 is a common factor too, but not the greatest. 168 is the LCM.

items.q: What is the greatest common factor (GCF) of 72 and 96?
items.e: Factors of 72: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 12, 18, 24, 36, 72. Factors of 96: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 96. Common factors: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. The greatest is 24. 12 is a common factor too, but not the greatest. 288 is the LCM.

items.q: What is the greatest common factor (GCF) of 17 and 51?
items.e: Factors of 17: 1, 17. Factors of 51: 1, 3, 17, 51. Common factors: 1, 17. The greatest is 17. 17 divides 51 (17 × 3 = 51), so the smaller number is the GCF.

items.q: What is the greatest common factor (GCF) of 25 and 36?
items.e: Factors of 25: 1, 5, 25. Factors of 36: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36. Common factors: 1. The greatest is 1. 25 and 36 share no factor except 1, so their GCF is 1.

items.q: What is the greatest common factor (GCF) of 108 and 144?
items.e: Factors of 108: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 27, 36, 54, 108. Factors of 144: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 12, 16, 18, 24, 36, 48, 72, 144. Common factors: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36. The greatest is 36. 18 is a common factor too, but not the greatest. 432 is the LCM.

items.q: What is the greatest common factor (GCF) of 84 and 126?
items.e: Factors of 84: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 12, 14, 21, 28, 42, 84. Factors of 126: 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 9, 14, 18, 21, 42, 63, 126. Common factors: 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 14, 21, 42. The greatest is 42. 21 is a common factor too, but not the greatest. 252 is the LCM.

items.q: Use the factor trees. What is the GCF of 60 and 84?
items.e: The trees give 60 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 5 and 84 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 7. Both lists share 2 × 2 × 3. Multiply the shared primes: 2 × 2 × 3 = 12. Using each shared prime only once gives 6, which is too small. 420 is the LCM.

items.q: Use the factor trees. What is the GCF of 72 and 108?
items.e: The trees give 72 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 and 108 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 3. Both lists share 2 × 2 × 3 × 3. Multiply the shared primes: 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 = 36. Using each shared prime only once gives 6, which is too small. 216 is the LCM.

items.q: Use the factor trees. What is the GCF of 90 and 126?
items.e: The trees give 90 = 2 × 3 × 3 × 5 and 126 = 2 × 3 × 3 × 7. Both lists share 2 × 3 × 3. Multiply the shared primes: 2 × 3 × 3 = 18. Using each shared prime only once gives 6, which is too small. 630 is the LCM.

items.q: Use the factor trees. What is the GCF of 48 and 120?
items.e: The trees give 48 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 and 120 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 5. Both lists share 2 × 2 × 2 × 3. Multiply the shared primes: 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 = 24. Using each shared prime only once gives 6, which is too small. 240 is the LCM.

Circle the primes in both lists: 2 × 2 × 2 × 2. Multiply them: 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 16. Use a shared prime as many times as it appears in both lists. 560 is the LCM, and 70 uses every prime, not only the shared ones.

items.q: 98 = 2 × 7 × 7 and 140 = 2 × 2 × 5 × 7. What is the GCF of 98 and 140?
items.e: Circle the primes in both lists: 2 × 7. Multiply them: 2 × 7 = 14. Use a shared prime as many times as it appears in both lists. 980 is the LCM, and 70 uses every prime, not only the shared ones.

items.q: What is the GCF of 40, 60 and 72?
items.e: Common factors of 40, 60 and 72: 1, 2, 4. The GCF is 4. The GCF of 40 and 60 alone is 20, but 20 is not a factor of 72. Check all three numbers.

items.q: What is the GCF of 48, 72 and 80?
items.e: Common factors of 48, 72 and 80: 1, 2, 4, 8. The GCF is 8. The GCF of 48 and 72 alone is 24, but 24 is not a factor of 80. Check all three numbers.

items.q: Lucas says the GCF of 36 and 90 is 9, because 9 is a factor of both. Is he right?
items.e: 9 is a common factor, but not the greatest. 18 × 2 = 36 and 18 × 5 = 90, so the GCF is 18. 180 is the LCM, and 36 is not a factor of 90.

items.q: Hana says the GCF of 27 and 108 is 27. Is she right?
items.e: 27 × 4 = 108, so 27 is a factor of both numbers, and no factor of 27 is bigger than 27. The GCF can be the smaller number.

items.q: Amira says 35 and 64 have no common factor, so they have no GCF. Is she right?
items.e: 1 is a factor of every whole number, so 1 is always a common factor. 35 = 5 × 7 and 64 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 share no prime, so the GCF is 1.

items.q: Which pair of numbers has a GCF of 12?
items.e: 36 = 12 × 3 and 60 = 12 × 5, and 3 and 5 share no factor, so the GCF of 36 and 60 is 12. The GCF of 24 and 48 is 24, of 3 and 4 is 1 (12 is their LCM), and of 30 and 42 is 6.

items.q: Which list shows the first five multiples of 7?
items.e: Multiply 7 by 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5: 7, 14, 21, 28, 35. The first multiple of a number is the number itself, not 0. Count by 7, not by 10, and don’t mix up multiples with factors.

items.q: Which list shows the first five multiples of 12?
items.e: Multiply 12 by 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5: 12, 24, 36, 48, 60. The first multiple of a number is the number itself, not 0. Count by 12, not by 10, and don’t mix up multiples with factors.

items.q: Which number is a multiple of 9?
items.e: 9 × 13 = 117, so 117 is a multiple of 9. 3 is a factor of 9, not a multiple. 89 ÷ 9 and 129 ÷ 9 have remainders. Ending in 9 does not make a number a multiple of 9.

items.q: Which number is a multiple of 12?
items.e: 12 × 11 = 132, so 132 is a multiple of 12. 6 is a factor of 12, not a multiple. 122 ÷ 12 and 112 ÷ 12 have remainders. Ending in 2 does not make a number a multiple of 12.

items.q: Which number is a multiple of 14?
items.e: 14 × 7 = 98, so 98 is a multiple of 14. 7 is a factor of 14, not a multiple. 104 ÷ 14 and 124 ÷ 14 have remainders. Ending in 4 does not make a number a multiple of 14.

items.q: Which number is not a multiple of 8?
Which statement is true?
items.e: 24 × 2 = 48, so 48 is a multiple of 24, and 24 is a factor of 48. A factor is never bigger than the number; a multiple is never smaller.

items.q: Which numbers in the picture are common multiples of 4 and 6?
items.e: Look for numbers in both rows. Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36. Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36. The common multiples shown are 12, 24, 36. Not only 4 × 6 = 24: 12 and 36 are in both rows too.

items.q: Which numbers in the picture are common multiples of 6 and 9?
items.e: Look for numbers in both rows. Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36, 42, 48, 54. Multiples of 9: 9, 18, 27, 36, 45, 54. The common multiples shown are 18, 36, 54. Not only 6 × 9 = 54: 18 and 36 are in both rows too.

items.q: Which numbers in the picture are common multiples of 8 and 12?
items.e: Look for numbers in both rows. Multiples of 8: 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48. Multiples of 12: 12, 24, 36, 48. The common multiples shown are 24, 48. 36 is a multiple of 12 only, and 16 is a multiple of 8 only.

items.q: Which numbers in the picture are common multiples of 5 and 8?
items.e: Look for numbers in both rows. Multiples of 5: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40. Multiples of 8: 8, 16, 24, 32, 40. The only common multiple shown is 40. 5 and 8 share no factor except 1, so their first common multiple is 5 × 8.

items.q: Which list shows all the multiples of 15 between 40 and 100?
items.e: Count by 15: 15, 30, 45, 60, 75, 90, 105. The ones between 40 and 100 are 45, 60, 75, 90. 30 is less than 40, and counting by 10 gives multiples of 10, not 15.

items.q: Which list shows the first three common multiples of 6 and 8?
items.e: The LCM of 6 and 8 is 24. The common multiples are the multiples of the LCM: 24, 48, 72. Counting by 6 × 8 = 48 skips 24.

items.q: Which list shows the first three common multiples of 9 and 12?
items.e: The LCM of 9 and 12 is 36. The common multiples are the multiples of the LCM: 36, 72, 108. Counting by 9 × 12 = 108 skips 36.

items.q: Which list shows the first three common multiples of 10 and 15?
items.e: The LCM of 10 and 15 is 30. The common multiples are the multiples of the LCM: 30, 60, 90. Counting by 10 × 15 = 150 skips 30.

items.q: Which number is a common multiple of 6 and 15?
items.e: 90 = 6 × 15 and 90 = 15 × 6, so 90 is a common multiple. 21 is 6 + 15. 45 and 36 are each a multiple of only one of the numbers.

items.q: Which number is a common multiple of 8 and 12?
items.e: 72 = 8 × 9 and 72 = 12 × 6, so 72 is a common multiple. 20 is 8 + 12. 64 and 36 are each a multiple of only one of the numbers.

items.q: Which number is a common multiple of 9 and 15?
items.e: 90 = 9 × 10 and 90 = 15 × 6, so 90 is a common multiple. 24 is 9 + 15. 60 and 81 are each a multiple of only one of the numbers.

items.q: Which number is not a common multiple of 6 and 10?
items.e: 40 is a multiple of 10, but 40 ÷ 6 = 6 R 4, so 40 is not a multiple of 6. The LCM of 6 and 10 is 30, and 30, 60 and 120 are all multiples of 30.

items.q: Olivia says the common multiples of 4 and 6 are 24, 48, 72, …, because 4 × 6 = 24. Is she right?
items.e: Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18, 24. 12 is also a multiple of 4. So the common multiples are 12, 24, 36, 48, … Counting by 4 × 6 = 24 misses 12, 36, …

sets.title: Lowest common multiple (LCM) of two or three numbers

items.q: What is the lowest common multiple (LCM) of 6 and 8?
items.e: Count by 8: 8, 16, 24. The first one that is also a multiple of 6 is 24. 6 × 8 = 48 is a common multiple, but not the lowest. 2 is the GCF.

items.q: What is the lowest common multiple (LCM) of 9 and 12?
items.e: Count by 12: 12, 24, 36. The first one that is also a multiple of 9 is 36. 9 × 12 = 108 is a common multiple, but not the lowest. 3 is the GCF.

items.q: What is the lowest common multiple (LCM) of 10 and 15?
items.e: Count by 15: 15, 30. The first one that is also a multiple of 10 is 30. 10 × 15 = 150 is a common multiple, but not the lowest. 5 is the GCF.

items.q: What is the lowest common multiple (LCM) of 12 and 18?
items.e: Count by 18: 18, 36. The first one that is also a multiple of 12 is 36. 12 × 18 = 216 is a common multiple, but not the lowest. 6 is the GCF.

items.q: What is the lowest common multiple (LCM) of 8 and 14?
items.e: Count by 14: 14, 28, 42, 56. The first one that is also a multiple of 8 is 56. 8 × 14 = 112 is a common multiple, but not the lowest. 2 is the GCF.

items.q: What is the lowest common multiple (LCM) of 7 and 9?
items.e: Count by 9: 9, 18, 27, 36, 45, 54, 63. The first one that is also a multiple of 7 is 63. 7 and 9 share no factor except 1, so here the LCM is 7 × 9.

items.q: What is the lowest common multiple (LCM) of 15 and 20?
items.e: Count by 20: 20, 40, 60. The first one that is also a multiple of 15 is 60. 15 × 20 = 300 is a common multiple, but not the lowest. 5 is the GCF.

items.q: What is the lowest common multiple (LCM) of 16 and 24?
items.e: Count by 24: 24, 48. The first one that is also a multiple of 16 is 48. 16 × 24 = 384 is a common multiple, but not the lowest. 8 is the GCF.

items.q: 18 = 2 × 3 × 3 and 30 = 2 × 3 × 5. What is the LCM of 18 and 30?
items.e: Use each prime the greatest number of times it appears in either list: 2 × 3 × 3 × 5 = 90. 18 × 30 = 540 uses the shared primes twice.

items.q: 20 = 2 × 2 × 5 and 24 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3. What is the LCM of 20 and 24?
items.e: Use each prime the greatest number of times it appears in either list: 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 5 = 120. 20 × 24 = 480 uses the shared primes twice.

items.q: What is the LCM of 2, 3 and 4?
items.e: Count by the biggest number, 4: 4, 8, 12. The first one that 2 and 3 also divide is 12. 2 × 3 × 4 = 24 is a common multiple, but not the lowest. 6 is the LCM of 2 and 3 only.

items.q: What is the LCM of 3, 4 and 6?
items.e: Count by the biggest number, 6: 6, 12. The first one that 3 and 4 also divide is 12. 3 × 4 × 6 = 72 is a common multiple, but not the lowest.

items.q: What is the LCM of 4, 5 and 6?
items.e: Count by the biggest number, 6: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36, 42, 48, 54, 60. The first one that 4 and 5 also divide is 60. 4 × 5 × 6 = 120 is a common multiple, but not the lowest. 20 is the LCM of 4 and 5 only.

items.q: What is the LCM of 6, 8 and 12?
items.e: Count by the biggest number, 12: 12, 24. The first one that 6 and 8 also divide is 24. 6 × 8 × 12 = 576 is a common multiple, but not the lowest.

items.q: What is the LCM of 3, 5 and 9?
items.e: Count by the biggest number, 9: 9, 18, 27, 36, 45. The first one that 3 and 5 also divide is 45. 3 × 5 × 9 = 135 is a common multiple, but not the lowest. 15 is the LCM of 3 and 5 only.

items.q: What is the LCM of 4, 6 and 10?
items.e: Count by the biggest number, 10: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60. The first one that 4 and 6 also divide is 60. 4 × 6 × 10 = 240 is a common multiple, but not the lowest. 12 is the LCM of 4 and 6 only.

items.q: Ava says the LCM of 4, 6 and 8 is 192, because 4 × 6 × 8 = 192. Is she right?
items.e: Count by 8: 8, 16, 24. 24 ÷ 4 = 6 and 24 ÷ 6 = 4, so the LCM is 24. 192 is a common multiple, but not the lowest. 2 is the GCF, and 48 is the LCM × 2.

items.q: Leah says the LCM of 6 and 9 is 3. Is she right?
c: No. 3 is the GCF. The LCM is 18
items.e: 3 is the greatest common factor. A multiple can’t be smaller than the numbers. Count by 9: 9, 18. 18 = 6 × 3, so the LCM is 18.

items.q: Emma says the LCM of 5, 10 and 20 is 20. Is she right?
items.e: 20 = 5 × 4 and 20 = 10 × 2, so 20 is a multiple of all three numbers, and no smaller multiple of 20 exists. The LCM is 20. When the biggest number is a multiple of the others, it is the LCM.

items.q: Which three numbers have an LCM of 30?
items.e: 30 = 3 × 10 = 5 × 6 = 10 × 3, and no smaller number is a multiple of 3, 5 and 10. So the answer is 3, 5 and 10. The LCM of 4, 5 and 6 is 60, of 3, 6 and 9 is 18, and of 2, 3 and 6 is 6.

items.q: Hot dogs come in packs of 12 and buns come in packs of 8. Ethan wants the same number of hot dogs and buns for the class barbecue. What is the least number of each he can buy?
items.e: Count by 12: 12, 24. The first one that is also a multiple of 8 is 24. So he buys 24 of each. 12 × 8 = 96 also works, but it is not the least. 4 is the GCF, and 20 is 12 + 8.

items.q: Hot dogs come in packs of 12 and buns come in packs of 8. Mateo buys the least number of packs so that there is a bun for every hot dog, with none left over. How many packs of buns does he buy?
items.e: The LCM of 12 and 8 is 24, so he needs 24 buns: 24 ÷ 8 = 3 packs. 2 packs is the number of packs of hot dogs (24 ÷ 12).

items.q: The school has 96 blue chairs and 72 red chairs for an assembly in the gym. Each row has only one colour, and every row has the same number of chairs. What is the greatest number of chairs in each row?
items.e: The row size must divide both 96 and 72. Common factors: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. The GCF is 24. 12 and 8 also work, but they are not the greatest. 288 is the LCM.

items.q: 96 blue chairs and 72 red chairs are set out in rows of 24, and each row has only one colour. How many rows are there?
items.e: 96 ÷ 24 = 4 blue rows and 72 ÷ 24 = 3 red rows. 4 + 3 = 7 rows. 24 is the number of chairs in each row. 21 rows would be rows of 8. 168 is the total number of chairs.

items.q: The Route 5 bus leaves the station every 12 minutes. The Route 9 bus leaves every 18 minutes. Both buses leave at 7:00 a.m. When will they next leave at the same time?
items.e: Count by 18: 18, 36. The first one that is also a multiple of 12 is 36. So they leave together again 36 minutes later, at 7:36 a.m. 12 × 18 = 216 minutes (10:36 a.m.) is not the first time. 30 is 12 + 18, and 6 is the GCF.

items.q: Three city buses leave the same stop every 10, 15 and 20 minutes. All three leave at 8:00 a.m. When will all three next leave together?
items.e: Count by 20: 20, 40, 60. 60 is also a multiple of 10 and of 15, so the LCM is 60 minutes, and they leave together at 9:00 a.m. 8:30 a.m. works for the first two buses only. 45 is 10 + 15 + 20, and 5 is the GCF.

items.q: For the Terry Fox Run, Maya has 120 water bottles and 84 granola bars. She packs identical snack bags with nothing left over. What is the greatest number of bags she can make?
items.e: The number of bags must divide both 120 and 84. Common factors: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. The GCF is 12. 840 is the LCM, and 7 is the number of granola bars in each bag.

items.q: A bulletin board is 90 cm by 144 cm. The class covers it with equal squares of paper, as large as possible, with no gaps or overlaps. What is the side length of each square?
items.e: The side must divide both 90 and 144. Common factors: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18. The GCF is 18 cm, which gives 5 rows of 8 squares. 720 is the LCM, and it is bigger than the board.

items.q: Priya has two ropes for a canoe trip, 105 cm and 135 cm long. She cuts both into pieces of the same length, as long as possible, with nothing left over. How long is each piece?
items.e: The length must divide both 105 and 135. Common factors: 1, 3, 5, 15. The GCF is 15 cm: 7 pieces from the first rope and 9 from the second. 945 is the LCM.

items.q: The Grade 7 classes have 28 boys and 42 girls. The teachers make teams for a soccer tournament. Each team has the same number of boys and the same number of girls, and no one is left out. What is the greatest number of teams?
items.e: Find the GCF of 28 and 42. Common factors: 1, 2, 7, 14. The GCF is 14, so there are 14 teams, each with 2 boys and 3 girls. 7 teams also works, but it is not the greatest. 70 is the total number of students, and 84 is the LCM.

items.q: At the skating rink, Sofia skates one lap every 40 seconds and Mei skates one lap every 60 seconds. They start together. After how many seconds are they both back at the start together?
items.e: Count by 60: 60, 120. The first one that is also a multiple of 40 is 120. That is 2 minutes. 40 × 60 = 2400 is not the first time, 100 is 40 + 60, and 20 is the GCF.

items.q: Three lights on a parade float flash every 4, 6 and 9 seconds. They flash together now. In how many seconds will all three next flash together?
items.e: Count by 9: 9, 18, 27, 36. 36 = 4 × 9 and 36 = 6 × 6, so the LCM is 36 seconds. 4 × 6 × 9 = 216 is not the first time. 12 works for the first two lights only, and 19 is 4 + 6 + 9.

items.q: For a picnic, hot dogs come in packs of 12, buns in packs of 8 and juice boxes in packs of 6. Nathan wants the same number of each, as few as possible. How many of each does he buy?
items.e: Count by 12: 12, 24. 24 is also a multiple of 8 and of 6, so the LCM is 24. 12 × 8 × 6 = 576 is far more than needed, 26 is 12 + 8 + 6, and 2 is the GCF.

items.q: Liam packs 24 granola bars, 36 apples and 60 juice boxes for a class field trip. Every bag must be identical, with nothing left over. What is the greatest number of bags?
items.e: Common factors of 24, 36 and 60: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. The GCF is 12, so each bag has 2 granola bars, 3 apples and 5 juice boxes. 6 and 4 also work, but they are not the greatest. 360 is the LCM.

items.q: Owen has hockey practice every 4 days and swimming lessons every 6 days. Both are on March 1. What is the next date when he has both?
items.e: The LCM of 4 and 6 is 12, so both happen again 12 days later: March 1 + 12 days = March 13. March 25 uses 4 × 6 = 24 days, March 11 uses 4 + 6 = 10 days, and March 3 uses the GCF, 2.

items.q: Benjamin makes the greatest number of identical gift bags from 45 pencils and 75 erasers, with nothing left over. How many erasers are in each bag?
items.e: The GCF of 45 and 75 is 15, so there are 15 bags. 75 ÷ 15 = 5 erasers in each bag (and 45 ÷ 15 = 3 pencils). 15 is the number of bags. 25 would come from using only 3 bags.

items.q: Star stickers come in sheets of 15 and heart stickers come in sheets of 20. Jayden wants the same number of star and heart stickers, as few as possible. How many of each does he get?
items.e: Count by 20: 20, 40, 60. The first one that is also a multiple of 15 is 60. That is 4 sheets of stars and 3 sheets of hearts. 15 × 20 = 300 is not the least, 5 is the GCF, and 35 is 15 + 20.

items.q: A teacher sets out 72 chairs and 54 desks in rows. Every row has the same number of items, and each row has only chairs or only desks. To find the most items in each row, what should you find?
items.e: The row size must divide both numbers, and it must be as big as possible. That is the GCF (18).

items.q: One bus leaves every 14 minutes and another leaves every 21 minutes. To find when they next leave together, what should you find?
items.e: The times repeat and must line up again, so you need a common multiple: the LCM (42 minutes). 14 × 21 = 294 is a common multiple, but not the first.

items.q: Hot dogs come in packs of 10 and buns in packs of 8. Kai says he must buy 80 of each so that every hot dog has a bun. Is he right?
items.e: Count by 10: 10, 20, 30, 40. The first one that is also a multiple of 8 is 40. So 4 packs of hot dogs and 5 packs of buns give 40 of each. 80 also works, but it is not the least. 18 is 10 + 8, and 2 is the GCF.
